subtopics: Reliability of Wikipedia: key academic studies comparing Wikipedia accuracy to traditional encyclopedias (e.g., the 2005 Nature study and later replications), with findings and criticisms
Wikipedia's editorial model: core content policies (verifiability, no original research, neutral point of view), editing community, and quality-control mechanisms
Criticism of Wikipedia: vandalism, systemic bias, gender gap, coverage gaps, and notable incidents affecting accuracy
How Wikipedia is viewed as a source in academic and professional research: guidance on citing Wikipedia, its tertiary-source status, and Wikipedia's own recommendations about citing it
